{{Infobox deity}}

[[Image:Descendants of izanagi alone.svg|thumb|right|200px|Deities born from Izanagi's purification ritual (based on the ''Kojiki'') [//upload.wikimedia.org/]]]

'''Kamunaobi no Kami''' (神直日神) is a {{ill|Kami|en|Kami|qid=Q524158|lt=Deity}} appearing in {{ill|Japanese mythology|en|Japanese mythology|qid=Q814158|lt=Japanese mythology}}.<ref name="T">[[Atsushi Yamakita]] ''Dictionary of Eastern Deities,'' {{ill|Shinkigensha|ja|新紀元社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinkigensha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11503908}}, p. 349.</ref> 
This deity is regarded as one who purifies defilements and rectifies calamities (禍, ''maga''). In the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'', the deity is referred to as '''Kamunaobi no Kami''' (神直毘神), while in the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'', it is written as '''Kamunaobi no Kami''' (神直日神). The name also appears as '''Kamunaobi no Kami''' (神直備神) in some texts.

== Overview ==
During the {{ill|Kamiumi|en|Kamiumi|qid=Q3545159|lt=birth of deities}}, when {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊邪那岐命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}} returned from {{ill|Yomi|en|Yomi|qid=Q1142558|lt=Yomi}}, the defilements of the underworld gave rise to the deity {{ill|Magatsuhi-no-kami|ja|禍津日神|lt=Magatsuhi no Kami}}. To rectify the calamities caused by Magatsuhi no Kami, '''Kamunaobi no Kami''' was born as one of the {{ill|Ōnaobi no Kami|ja|直毘神|lt=Naobi no Kami}}. Following this, a second deity, '''Ōnaobi no Kami''' (大直日神), was born, and finally {{ill|Izunome|ja|伊豆能売|zh|伊豆能賣神|qid=Q10885126}} was born.

== Analysis ==
According to the scholar {{ill|Shinobu Orikuchi|arz|شينوبو اوريكوكى|de|Orikuchi Shinobu|fr|Shinobu Orikuchi|hy|Սինոբու Օրիգուտի|ja|折口信夫|ru|Орикути, Синобу|qid=Q3482286|lt=Shinobu Orikuchi}}, the following interpretations have been proposed:<ref name="U">{{ill|Shinobu Orikuchi|arz|شينوبو اوريكوكى|de|Orikuchi Shinobu|fr|Shinobu Orikuchi|hy|Սինոբու Օրիգուտի|ja|折口信夫|ru|Орикути, Синобу|qid=Q3482286|lt=Shinobu Orikuchi}}, ''Collected Works of Shinobu Orikuchi (New Edition),'' {{ill|Chuokoron-Shinsha|en|Chuokoron-Shinsha|qid=Q996095|lt=Chūōkōron-shinsha}}.</ref> 
* The ''Naobi'' deity was conceptualized as a counterpart to Magatsuhi no Kami, representing two sides of the same coin. The {{ill|Ōnaobi no Kami|ja|直毘神|lt=Naobi no Kami}} is seen as the priest who performs purification rituals, while Izunome is considered a shamaness (miko).
* The verb ''naoru'' (to correct or heal) is related to the "直" (nao) in ''Naobi no Kami,'' symbolizing a deity that corrects mistakes or restores balance.
* During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, Naobi no Kami was revered as a deity of banquets and entertainment.

==Merged second translation==
[[Image:Descendants of izanagi alone.svg|thumb|right|200px|Deities born from Izanagi's purification (based on the Kojiki) [//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d3/Creation_myths_of_Japan_5.svg View in SVG (supported browsers only)]]]]
'''Kamunaobi no Kami''' (神直日神, also spelled かむなおひのかみ) is a deity in {{ill|Shinto|en|Shinto|qid=Q812767|lt=Shinto}}.<ref name="T">[[Atsushi Yamakita]] 『東洋神名事典』 {{ill|Gakken|en|Gakken|qid=Q2664679|lt=Gakken}} p. 349.</ref> This deity is said to purify defilements and rectify {{ill|Magatsuhi-no-kami|ja|禍|lt=Magatsuhi}} (misfortunes or evils). In the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}, the deity is referred to as Kamunaobi no Kami (神直毘神), while the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} refers to the deity as Kamunaohi no Kami (神直日神). Other texts also spell the name as Kamunaobi no Kami (神直備神).

== Overview ==
During the {{ill|Kamiumi|en|Kamiumi|qid=Q3545159|lt=Birth of the Gods}}, {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊邪那岐命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}} returned from {{ill|Yomi|en|Yomi|qid=Q1142558|lt=Yomi}}, where defilements from Yomi gave rise to {{ill|Magatsuhi-no-kami|ja|禍津日神|lt=Magatsuhi no Kami}}. To counteract the calamities caused by Magatsuhi no Kami, Kamunaobi no Kami was born as one of the {{ill|Ōnaobi no Kami|ja|直毘神|lt=Naobi no Kami}}. Subsequently, another deity, {{ill|Ōnaobi no Kami|ja|大直毘神}}, was born, followed by {{ill|Izunome|ja|伊豆能売|zh|伊豆能賣神|qid=Q10885126}}.

== Historical Interpretations ==
According to {{ill|Shinobu Orikuchi|arz|شينوبو اوريكوكى|de|Orikuchi Shinobu|fr|Shinobu Orikuchi|hy|Սինոբու Օրիգուտի|ja|折口信夫|ru|Орикути, Синобу|qid=Q3482286|lt=Shinobu Orikuchi}}, Kamunaobi no Kami has the following attributes:<ref name="U">{{ill|Shinobu Orikuchi|arz|شينوبو اوريكوكى|de|Orikuchi Shinobu|fr|Shinobu Orikuchi|hy|Սինոբու Օրիգուտի|ja|折口信夫|ru|Орикути, Синобу|qid=Q3482286|lt=Shinobu Orikuchi}} 『折口信夫全集 新版』 [[:en:Chūōkōron-sha|Chūōkōron-sha]].</ref>  
* Naobi no Kami is considered a paired and interconnected deity with Magatsuhi no Kami, embodying their dual aspects. Additionally, Kamunaobi no Kami functions as the officiant deity in purification rituals, while Izunome is considered the miko (shrine maiden).  
* The term "naoru" (to rectify or correct) is linguistically related to the "Nao" (直) in Kamunaobi no Kami, implying a deity invoked to rectify missteps or wrongdoings.  
* By the Heian period, Kamunaobi no Kami was associated with being a deity of feasts or entertainment.
